newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt Nov pax up 3.1pct, rivals win traffic.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt Nov pax up 3.1pct, rivals win traffic.

text.p: Passenger traffic at Frankfurt airport picked up in November with a 3.1 percent rise to 2.94 million passengers due to increasing international travel, airport authority figures showed.
But domestic traffic was hit by improved connections between regional German airports and leading European rivals, the latest Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) traffic report said.
Passenger growth last month was generated by foreign travel, in particular to tourist destinations in Turkey and North Africa.
North America passenger numbers also improved compared to previous months, the report noted.
"But domestic travel continued to develop negatively. Not only are there economic reasons but also a negative trend for connecting passengers from or to domestic (airports)," the report said.
"Seemingly, through the improved connection of German airports to foreign hubs (London, Paris, Zurich, Amsterdam), traffic is being diverted away from Frankfurt."
The number of transit passengers fell 3.7 percent last month and has fallen 5.8 percent year-on-year from January-November, the report showed.
Overall passenger numbers at Frankfurt airport have risen 1.6 percent to 36 million over the first 11 months of the year.
The average seat load factor improved slightly last month but remained below comparable 1995 levels, the report said.
The number of flights stagnated in November at more than 30,000 but has risen two percent January-November, it added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
